Who it’s for

New teachersStruggling teachersMentorsAnyone who needs help organizing teaching

The question behind it

What does a teacher need to know and do right now?

Teaching is usually scattered across calendars, notes apps, folders, spreadsheets and chats. Mentor answers the everyday questions in one place: who am I teaching today, what happened in the last lesson, was the student present, what homework is due, where are the materials, and how much teaching have I done.

Scheduling

Day and week views, recurring lessons, templates and conflict warnings.

Planning

Lesson workflow, goals and tasks with priorities, due dates and progress.

Organization

Tagged and pinned notes, plus materials linked to students and lessons.

Responsibilities

Student profiles, attendance, homework with results, and statistics.

One workflow, start to finish

Schedule→Lesson→Attendance→Notes→Homework→Student history→Statistics

Under the hood

Python 3.12 and PySide6 (Qt) give a native desktop interface, SQLite stores everything relationally with no database server, and PyInstaller with Inno Setup builds the Windows installer. The code separates UI, services, data access, theme and localization, and the schema (now v4) is upgraded through versioned migrations so teaching data survives updates.

Python 3.12PySide6 / QtSQLitePyInstallerInno Setup

Quality is checked with compilation checks, database and service regression tests, and Qt offscreen smoke tests. The recorded 1.4 build ran 40 tests: 33 passed, none failed, and 7 Qt runtime cases were left for Windows and CI.

Designed to stay out of the way

Full dark mode with an orange accent, no permanent sidebar, and a floating glass dock with five destinations: Home, Schedule, Notes, Materials and Statistics. Accent, glass intensity, motion, density and glow are all adjustable, and animation is never allowed to compromise stability on modest hardware. Your data stays on your PC in SQLite, with backup, restore and JSON/CSV export, in English, O‘zbekcha and Русский.

What’s next

1.5 · Teaching Mode

Planned: a Start Lesson action with a timer, student context, previous homework, live notes, linked materials and a wrap-up flow.

1.6 · Advanced Calendar

Planned: drag to reschedule, resize durations, richer recurring series and stronger collision feedback.

The roadmap follows one rule: functionality, stability, UX, visual quality, animation, then extras.

Direction is more important than speed.

Mentor is built for a single local user and has no cloud sync yet. The installer isn’t code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may show an “Unknown publisher” warning on first launch.
